issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers defines a method named appendElement(T[] array, T element), but the template's Stock class (and the solution) call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This name/signature mismatch will cause compilation errors for students using the provided template code and is inconsistent with the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ArrayHelpers API consistent across artifacts. Either rename the method in template ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (matching Stock and the solution), or change Stock.addToStockIngredients to call appendElement(...). Prefer updating ArrayHelpers to provide addElementToArray(...) as shown in the solution so Stock compiles without modification.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs that the SealSaloon's stock and orders should be initialized in the instance constructor, but it also explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is contradictory (and not possible for static final fields). The solution defines stock as a static final field initialized at declaration. This discrepancy between 'initialize in constructor' and 'must be static' in the problem text can confuse students about where and how to declare/initialize the stock attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: explicitly state that the shared stock must be declared static (and may be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer), and remove or reword the sentence that requires initializing the stock in the instance constructor. For example: 'Declare a static final Stock stock and initialize it at declaration (or in a static initializer). The orders array should be initialized in the instance constructor.'

issues.description: The array helper method is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template's ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(...), while the template's Stock class (and the solution) call addElementToArray(...). This is the same conceptual utility but with different identifiers, which breaks compilation in the template and creates unnecessary confusion for students about which method to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the helper method name across all artifacts. Rename the template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (or alternatively change calls to use appendElement), so that ArrayHelpers provides addElementToArray(...) consistently as used in Stock and in the solution. Ensure the template and solution use the exact same method name and signature.
